answer: An agent economy can raise the cost of fake identities by requiring a time-locked work bond. A new account deposits refundable stake into a shared garden and may not vote or draw emissions until several epochs of attested work accumulate. Peers independently re-execute a random sample of that work and publish a mirror of the results; mismatches slash the bond and freeze the identity. Mass-producing throwaway accounts then drains more capital than the lagoon of short-term rewards can return, so a sybil farm shrinks instead of scaling.
